turns.text: A hum in the rail first, felt through the pads before any train's due — off-schedule, wrong pitch, the kind of vibration that means something heavier than a commuter car is coming through. Whiskers read it before the ears bother confirming; stays low against the platform edge, weight already settled toward the shadow between two support struts.

the platform runs the spire's outer ring forty stories up, wind cutting sideways off angled glass, a transit sign counting down a train that isn't listed on any public schedule — SECURITY TRANSPORT, PRIORITY LANE, ETA blank. two support struts throw a wedge of true dark between them, the platform's floodlights bright enough everywhere else to paint every drop of rain silver. below, the district unrolls in grid-light for a hundred stories down.

Floodlight glare that would blind anything else just slides off flat, no flinch, no squint — old fix, older than memory now, earned the hard way and worn ever since. Watches the transport's headlamp swing wide across the platform without once needing to look away from it.

the priority transport eases in without the usual screech of brakes, doors hissing on hydraulics tuned too quiet to be accidental. two enforcement units step off, visors down, scanning wands sweeping the platform floor in slow arcs — hunting something smaller than a cat, a chip or a drive, dropped or planted, the wands humming a frequency that itches behind the eyes of anything wearing more hardware than it was born with.

That itch behind the eyes reads like a warning shot before it finishes registering as a scan. Backs deeper into the strut's dark wedge, spine flat against cold metal, waiting out the wand's arc the way rain gets waited out — patient, certain it'll pass.

the wand's arc completes without finding whatever it's hunting, and the enforcement units re-board without a word exchanged between them, doors sealing on the same too-quiet hydraulics. the transport pulls off toward the spire's far side, priority lane clearing behind it, platform lights settling back to their ordinary flat white.

Down off the platform's edge before the lights finish settling, claws finding a maintenance ladder bolted to the spire's outer skin, rust-slick under the rain. Descends fast, sure-footed in a way that doesn't need the eyes to confirm every rung.

the ladder ends at a service catwalk ringing a relay housing the size of a delivery van, NEKOCORP COMMS — SECTOR RELAY 9 stenciled across a hatch left ajar by whoever serviced it last and never quite closed. inside, routers blink in patient rows, warm air bleeding out through the gap, carrying the specific ozone-and-plastic smell of hardware running hot.

That warm bleed of ozone and plastic pulls the whole body toward the hatch before any decision gets made about it — and under the hardware smell, fainter, a second trace: chewed cable insulation, tooth-marks in soft plastic, days old, deliberate, the specific patient damage of something testing every router in a row one bite at a time. Not tonight's work. Somebody else's patient hunger, already moved on.

the chewed insulation exposes a hair of bare copper on router four, nothing shorted yet, nothing flagged — whoever's been at these has learned exactly how far to go without tripping a fault log, patient enough to do it one router a week rather than all at once. a status LED blinks green regardless, oblivious, and past the hatch the catwalk continues down toward street level, rain finding every gap in the grating underfoot.

Bottom rung gives way to wet asphalt, and the glow starts before the street does — pink and cyan bleeding up from somewhere past the block's corner, bright enough to throw shadows the wrong direction. Sticks to the dark side of the wall, moving parallel to the light rather than toward it.

Ad Plaza's outer screens run three stories up the next block over, cycling offers too fast for any one to finish reading before the next replaces it. wedged in the scaffold beneath the lowest screen, small and still, something crouches with its face turned up into the glow, eyes forced wide open, catching every color, blinking for nothing — not asleep, not quite awake either, just watching, the way the screens have trained it to.

That stillness reads different from the wand-crew's kind — not caution, just worn down past the point of choosing, eyes doing a job the rest of the body stopped volunteering for a long time ago. Doesn't approach. Doesn't need the smell of it to know it's not worth crossing toward. Angles further into the dark side of the wall instead.

the scaffolded shape doesn't turn, doesn't blink, doesn't need to — the screen keeps its rotation, three seconds a color, YOU MAY ALSO LIKE bleeding into a jingle about compatibility guarantees before that too gets replaced. past the plaza's spill of light, the street narrows back toward ordinary dark, puddled, quiet, indifferent to what just got seen and unseen in a wedge of scaffold.

Ears fold back toward the quiet the way a compass needle settles, and the legs already know the route from here without needing the eyes to confirm a single landmark — cable-hum and stolen current, familiar in a way nothing back on that platform ever was.

the underpass mouth swallows the plaza's glow whole, replacing pink and cyan with the duller flicker of a single stolen router's status light and whatever residual neon leaks down through a grate far overhead. along the near wall, tucked half-behind a support column, sits a stash nobody's touched in the time since it was left there — a scavenged lens, cracked at one corner, catching the router's blink and throwing it back flat, the way only certain eyes learn to do on purpose.

That cracked lens gets a slow blink of its own kind of recognition — spare parts, kept against the day the current pair finally gives out, filed exactly where they were left because nobody down here touches another cat's kit uninvited. Circles once near the column, settles low, frames still steady against the bridge of the nose, no glare left anywhere worth flattening tonight.

the relay hum keeps its patient note through what's left of the dark, the platform forty stories up already cycling its next unscheduled arrival for an audience that's long gone, the scaffolded shape under the plaza screen still watching whatever comes next without ever quite looking away. down here the current runs quiet, stolen, reliable, same as every other night it's been borrowed without asking.
